newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 24.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** India's Congress party on Monday elected veteran leader Sitaram Kesri as its provisional president to take the place of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao who quit on Saturday after a court summons in a cheating case

** Top index-linked firms on the Bombay Stock Exchange are likely to see their sales growth shrinking to 9-10 percent in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) from 24 percent year ago, an Economic Times research poll says
It sees net profit slowing to 25 percent from 46
percent, with the worst hit being petrochemicals followed by aluminium and cement
The survey sees automobile and pharmaceutical firms
bucking the trend
** Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture of U.S. oil majors Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, plans to invest $5.0 billion in Asia by 2000, its chief says
New markets under consideration include China, Vietnam,
Cambodia, India and Indonesia

** About half a dozen foreign bidders including Japan's Mitsubishi and Mitsui have put in bids for a 37 percent stake in the loss-making state-owned Indian Iron and Steel Company which has planned a 43.48 billion rupees revival plan, the Finance Express reports

** Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the bourse regulator, permits banks and financial institutions to go ahead with their public offerings without giving any future financial projections, the Economic Times says
** The spot dollar/rupee INR= opened little changed at 35.72/73 per dollar and seen steady, dealers say
MARKETS:

** On Monday, shares across India finished lower in nervous trade with investors on the sidelines watchful of developments in the Congress party, the support of which is vital for the ruling minority coalition government
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index .BSESN closed 15.69 points, or 0.47 percent, lower at 3,331.09 after rising to 3,307.20
** The 100-share National index .NATEX fell 5.45 points, or 0.36 percent, at 1,489.00
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index .NSEI dropped 9.91 points to 968.84
** The 500-share CRISIL index was off 4.88 points, or 0.74 percent, at 651.63
** The Delhi share index slipped 6.14 points to 736.51
** The Calcutta index .CALSN fell 3.24 points to 428.83
** The Madras index .MDSI shed 20.99 points to 3,416.80
** The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index JCEAI slipped 0.73 points, or 1.06 percent, to 68.78 with the premium over the local market at 13.51 percent
